task:
Galaxy map nebulae: honest inventory, counts and a retained planetary-nebula class (review finding M02). apps/web only. Cloud appearance (M03) is a separate later task; do not redesign the cloud look here.

VERIFIED ON MAIN (e3aba577):
- The pinned asset `/assets/edastro-mapcharts-nebulae.json` has 5,842 records: 5,496 `planetary-nebula` and 346 `nebula` (`apps/web/src/lib/spatial/galaxy-nebulae.ts` `GalaxyNebula.kind`).
- `apps/web/src/lib/spatial/babylon/adapter.ts` `createGalaxyNebulaeMesh()` skips every `planetary-nebula`, keeps only the first `nebula` per rounded 1,400 LY cell (`NEBULA_LANDMARK_CELL_LY`) in file order, caps at 260 (`NEBULA_LANDMARK_LIMIT`); the result is 249 instances for this asset. The whole layer fades out from 8,000 LY and is hidden below 2,000 LY.
- `galaxyNebulaeReceipt()` sets BOTH `acceptedTargetCount` and `renderedTargetCount` to `payload.nebulae.length` (5,842), while 249 are rendered; `spatialLayer.renderedPointCount` is the real number. The Explore status line says "5,842 EDAstro nebula landmarks" (ExploreWorkspace.svelte ~line 1710).

WHAT TO DO:
1. Truthful counts: the receipt's `acceptedTargetCount` must equal the records accepted by the parser and `renderedTargetCount` must equal the instances actually in the scene for the current camera (0 when the layer is fully faded/hidden). Add explicit counts to the layer metadata: catalogue records, accepted features, landmarks selected, culled (deduplicated) entries, and currently visible, per kind. The Explore status line must distinguish "5,842 catalogue records" from "N landmarks shown" and, when the layer is faded out, say so instead of a count that implies they are on screen.
2. Planetary nebulae are a feature class, not junk: keep them as a separate close-range representation (for example a small, dim marker instance set that fades IN below a chosen camera distance where diffuse landmarks fade out, e.g. visible at <= 3,000 LY, and is hidden at galaxy overview), with its own metadata counts. Decide the exact band in the policy constants; do not use the diffuse-cloud radius for them. A dataset of only planetary nebulae must produce either this visible mode or an explicit "no landmarks at this zoom" status — never a silent nothing.
3. Landmark selection: keep stable identities (the same nebula wins its cell every time, independent of file order — choose by a deterministic significance rule such as the named/regional entry, then lowest id) so zooming and re-renders do not swap which landmark represents a cell. Keep the 260 cap and 1,400 LY cell as constants; make them explicit in metadata.
4. Keep the current sphere/material look, palette and fade band for diffuse clouds in this task; M03 replaces the cloud rendering later.

TESTS (vitest): receipt counts equal actual accepted/rendered against (a) the real 5,842-record asset via the existing `galaxy-nebulae` parse path and (b) tiny mixed fixtures (1 diffuse + 3 planetary; planetary only; empty); deterministic landmark choice per cell regardless of input order; planetary band visible/hidden at the chosen distances; Explore status text for the three cases (loaded at overview, loaded zoomed in, planetary-only). Existing tests must keep passing; update any that pinned the 5,842 rendered claim and say so in CHANGES.md.

VALIDATION: in apps/web run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`. CHANGES.md: one dated 2026-11-02 entry at the top; note the visible change needs Product E2E/visual validation before production promotion and is not deployed.
